How many orders fit in the window, what limits us, and what actually happened.

Step durations, batch sizes, unit kinds and resources come from
`task_planning_params` (or learned history where there is enough of it), so edits
in the planning settings move this report. Worker and machine counts default to
what is active in the database; hours and days per week are scenario knobs.

AmJobHistoryOut.title: AmJobHistoryOut
AmJobHistoryOut.description:
One completed AM job, enriched with the parts/teeth it produced — for the Production
History page's AM Job History tab.

AssignmentSectionEnum.title: AssignmentSectionEnum
AssignmentSectionEnum.description: Where a step sits in the order's assignment table (spec decision 19).

AvailablePreciousPowderOut.title: AvailablePreciousPowderOut
AvailablePreciousPowderOut.description:
Total precious powder physically on hand right now, for the AM Job History
tab's informational (non-KPI) tile — not date-filtered, since it's a snapshot of
current stock, not a historical aggregate.

Sums every non-retired PreciousPowderBatch's own remaining_amount (bulk stock not
yet loaded into a cartridge) plus every non-retired cartridge's remaining amount —
except a cartridge currently seated on equipment a job is actively holding
(resources.machine_held), since that powder is mid-consumption, not available.

CartridgeOutNested.title: CartridgeOutNested
CartridgeOutNested.description: Slim — no precious_powder back-ref. Used inside PreciousPowderBatchOut.

CartridgeUpdate.title: CartridgeUpdate
CartridgeUpdate.description:
current_weight is deliberately NOT updatable here.

It is owned by the AM_PREP fill and PART_POWDER_REMOVAL weigh-out, which write a
component_wear_ledger row for every gram. A generic PATCH would let the weight
move with no ledger entry, which makes the ledger unusable as the source of
truth for per-job powder. A manual correction needs its own audited endpoint.

CompleteTaskInput.title: CompleteTaskInput
CompleteTaskInput.description:
The wire-format schema: the union of every task_type's fields, all optional except
the base's. task.complete() validates the task_type-specific subset (see task_effects.
narrow_submit_input) internally; this stays wide so the API contract and generated
frontend client don't need a task_type-keyed discriminated union.

CompletedTaskDetailOut.title: CompletedTaskDetailOut
CompletedTaskDetailOut.description:
A finished WorkTask's configuration and stats.

Narrow on purpose rather than widening WorkTaskOut, which is the queue's payload and
already large. planned_params and submitted_params both survive completion — only
draft_params is cleared on terminal transitions.

FinishTaskInput.title: FinishTaskInput
FinishTaskInput.description:
Close an UNATTENDED task. An END TIME, not a duration: a print that finishes at
03:00 gets closed at 07:00, and the worker knows the clock time rather than the
elapsed minutes. Duration is derived.

Deliberately carries no is_successful flag: the finish button means the run is
OVER, not that it went well. Every linked part gets its own approve-or-scrap
verdict via `results` instead, so a run can partially advance and partially roll
back -- the whole-task success/failure is *derived* from those per-part outcomes
(see job_effects.derive_unattended_success), never asked of the worker directly.

HandoffTaskInput.title: HandoffTaskInput
HandoffTaskInput.description:
Submit for a has_handoff task: the same manual payload, plus how long the worker
expects the unattended run to take.

JobAssignmentRow.title: JobAssignmentRow
JobAssignmentRow.description: One job-level step of a print / mill job and who is assigned (job grain, #151).

JobCorrectionOut.title: JobCorrectionOut
JobCorrectionOut.description:
One job (AM, primary mill, or secondary mill), for one of the Jobs tab's
three tables. print_job_no is a comma-joined, deduplicated list for a mill job
whose plate/blank touches more than one order.

JobDetailOut.title: JobDetailOut
JobDetailOut.description:
Full detail of a WorkTask's linked Job (see MillJob/AmJob in
models/orders/production.py) — every base Job field plus every field of
whichever subclass job_kind names, not just the one fact (the milling blank)
the modal used to single out. Populated for every task with a job_id, whether it
created that job or finished it (see subjects.job_kind_for_task and
TaskBehaviour.owns_job_run) — the modal does not special-case which.

Resolved fresh from Job/MillJob/AmJob on every read (order_flow.completed_tasks_for_step),
never stored on WorkTask itself — same read-time-only shape as id_labels below.

JobPowderOut.title: JobPowderOut
JobPowderOut.description:
Precious powder moved in and out of cartridges for one job.

added_g — grams filled into cartridges at AM_PREP (summed; a job may be topped
    up more than once).
consumed_g — grams that had actually left the cartridge at PART_POWDER_REMOVAL.
added_g - consumed_g is what stayed in the cartridge and carries to the next job.
Both are derived from component_wear_ledger, so they stay correct however often
the same cartridge is reused.

JobTimeUpdate.title: JobTimeUpdate
JobTimeUpdate.description:
PATCH body for /process/job-time-correction/jobs/{job_id}. Only the fields
actually being corrected are sent -- read with model_dump(exclude_unset=True).

JobTimeUpdateOut.title: JobTimeUpdateOut
JobTimeUpdateOut.description:
PATCH response -- deliberately narrower than JobCorrectionOut. Recomputing
print_job_no after a correction would mean re-running the same lane-classification
query this job's own list endpoint already ran to find it in the first place; the
frontend already has that value from the row it clicked, so the response only
carries what actually changed and the caller merges it into the existing row.

MillJobHistoryOut.title: MillJobHistoryOut
MillJobHistoryOut.description:
One completed primary-lane mill job, enriched with the parts/teeth it milled and
the print job number of the order's AM (secondary) job — for the Production
History page's Milling Job History (Primary) tab.

NestingFlowEnum.title: NestingFlowEnum
NestingFlowEnum.description:
When an order reaches the external scheduler (scheduler integration, slice 7).
CLASSIC: once DATA_PREP_SECONDARY nested it (or, without secondary parts, once planned).
PLANNED: once planned; its nesting tasks are planned steps, with assumed plates until the nesting.

OrderAssignmentRow.title: OrderAssignmentRow

OrderAssignmentsPut.title: OrderAssignmentsPut
OrderAssignmentsPut.description:
Full replacement of the order's order-grain assignments: a step left out is
unassigned.

OrderFlowSectionEnum.title: OrderFlowSectionEnum
OrderFlowSectionEnum.description:
The sections the manufacturing flow is read in, matching the queue page's layout.

The backend assigns these rather than the frontend slicing them: REWORK_CHECKOUT is
ONE node (one PLATE-level task spanning both lanes), so it can carry only one
section. A frontend findIndex/slice would fail to find it in whichever lane did not
claim it and would dump that whole lane into pre-QM.

OrderFlowStepOut.title: OrderFlowStepOut
OrderFlowStepOut.description: One node of the order-level flow: a task type plus how far the order is through it.

OrderKpiOut.title: OrderKpiOut
OrderKpiOut.description:
One completed order — for the Production History page's Task History tab
order-level KPI row (Average Processing Time, Average Work Hours per
Order/Telescope, First Time Right Rate, Scrap Rate Primary/Secondary). Like
TaskHistoryOut, aggregation across orders and the shared date-range filter
(applied to completed_at) happen client-side, so these numbers stay a
sum-of-sums rather than an average-of-averages.

OrderProgress.title: OrderProgress
OrderProgress.description:
How many task types an order has cleared, out of how many it must clear.

Rendered as a fraction ("14/27"), never a percentage.

OrderScrapOut.title: OrderScrapOut
OrderScrapOut.description:
One scrapped part. `task_type` is the step it was scrapped at when resolvable;
otherwise `after_status` names the last status it produced.

OrderStageEnum.title: OrderStageEnum
OrderStageEnum.description:
A coarser, single-tag reading of an order's progress for the sales page —
where OrderFlowSectionEnum (below) is the per-lane sectioning the Process tab's
graph renders, this collapses PRIMARY_PRE_QM/SECONDARY_PRE_QM into one PRE_QM (and
the two *_FINISHING sections into one FINISHING_PARTS) since the sales page shows
one tag per order, not two lane columns. See services.process.progress.order_stage.

PartDetail.title: PartDetail
PartDetail.description:
One part as the start modal lists it. ReadyWork.part_details carries these keyed by
order_part_id -- the structured sibling of part_labels, which stays for the strips.

PartPlacementOut.title: PartPlacementOut
PartPlacementOut.description:
One print of one part on one build plate.

Derived, not stored: TaskPart.quadrant (the machine slot the part was assigned at
DATA_PREP_SECONDARY) joined against EquipmentComponentHistory (which plate held
that slot, and when). See app/services/process/placement.py.

PlanOrderFinishOut.title: PlanOrderFinishOut
PlanOrderFinishOut.description: The plan's computed finish of an order; never written to estimated_done_date.

PlanUpdatePendingOut.title: PlanUpdatePendingOut
PlanUpdatePendingOut.description:
*Plan update pending: n orders nested since hh:mm* (slice 7.4, planned nesting flow): orders whose nesting
finished after the last applied proposal was requested. The scheduler mapped them onto the plan without
re-optimizing; *Update plan* (a proposal without orders) is the re-solve. Empty in the classic flow.

PlannedBreakOut.title: PlannedBreakOut
PlannedBreakOut.description: A worker's break (spec decision 21): one per working day; the plan's steps leave it free.

PlannedStepOut.title: PlannedStepOut
PlannedStepOut.description:
One open step in the computed plan (ADR 0002): never stored, rebuilt on every read.

`key` is `order:<id>:<task type>` or, once data prep created its job, `job:<id>:<task type>`;
a scheduled plate step `carrier:<am job id>:<quadrant>:<task type>` (`services/planning/problem.py`).
`attended_end` is when the worker is free again; `end` includes the unattended run.

PreciousPowderBatchOutNested.title: PreciousPowderBatchOutNested
PreciousPowderBatchOutNested.description: Slim — no cartridges back-ref. Used inside CartridgeOut.

PrepSlotCandidateOut.title: PrepSlotCandidateOut
PrepSlotCandidateOut.description:
A component eligible to be installed into a slot. Base component fields plus the
subtype fields the prep pickers annotate — cartridge weights / precious batch, or a
drill's lot/diameter/remaining life. These are None for candidates of a different
subtype (the attribute simply does not exist there).

PrepSlotOut.title: PrepSlotOut
PrepSlotOut.description:
An equipment slot plus the components currently available to install into it:
matching component_type, not retired, not seated in any slot. Populated for every
slot regardless of occupancy so occupied slots still offer replacement candidates.

ProblemAssignmentOut.title: ProblemAssignmentOut
ProblemAssignmentOut.description: A planner's intent for an open node: inputs to the scheduler, never written by it.

ProblemCarrierOut.title: ProblemCarrierOut
ProblemCarrierOut.description:
One plate of one print: the parts nested together (AM job, quadrant). The physical plate is
not part of it; it is bound at AM_PREP.

ProblemOperationOut.title: ProblemOperationOut
ProblemOperationOut.description:
One step to plan. A job-level step is shared by every order on that job (`order_ids`);
a carrier step by every order with parts on that plate.

ProblemParamsOut.title: ProblemParamsOut
ProblemParamsOut.description:
One `task_planning_params` row: minutes = base + per_unit x units, units counted per
`unit_kind` (PART: tooth links, PART_COUNT: parts, PLATE: plates, ORDER: orders). The
operations' minutes are computed from these; the scheduler reads the step shape from them.

ProblemTaskOut.title: ProblemTaskOut
ProblemTaskOut.description: A started step: its task's facts; expected ends as the plan computes them while it runs.

ProcessAreaEnum.title: ProcessAreaEnum
ProcessAreaEnum.description: Where a task happens; the history timeline colours bars by it.

ProposalApply.title: ProposalApply
ProposalApply.description: The estimated done date per selected order; a missing one is the proposal's finish.

ProposalComparisonOut.title: ProposalComparisonOut
ProposalComparisonOut.description: The proposal against the plan served now (READY only): what applying it changes.

ProposalCreate.title: ProposalCreate
ProposalCreate.description: `POST /planning/proposals`: *Plan selected* (orders ready for planning) or, empty, *Update plan*.

ProposalOrderOut.title: ProposalOrderOut
ProposalOrderOut.description: One order's finish now and with the proposal applied.

ProposalStatusIn.title: ProposalStatusIn
ProposalStatusIn.description: The scheduler took a proposal (SOLVING) or gave up on it (FAILED, with why).

ProposalStepChangeOut.title: ProposalStepChangeOut
ProposalStepChangeOut.description: An open step the proposal gives another worker or machine, or moves while it starts today.

ReplanOrderOut.title: ReplanOrderOut
ReplanOrderOut.description: An order already past planning (PLANNED) and what is left to assign (decision 22).

ResourceKindEnum.title: ResourceKindEnum
ResourceKindEnum.description:
Capacity pools. WORKER is always charged a step's attended minutes; the other
members are the *machine* a step additionally occupies (attended + unattended).

RouteStepLookupOut.title: RouteStepLookupOut
RouteStepLookupOut.description: One selectable route step for the intern early-termination dropdown.

ScheduleIn.title: ScheduleIn
ScheduleIn.description: `PUT /planning/schedule`: one solve's result, stored as a new publication.

ScheduleStepIn.title: ScheduleStepIn
ScheduleStepIn.description: One step of a published schedule. `key` is the plan's node key.

ScrapRequest.title: ScrapRequest
ScrapRequest.description:
Scrap a whole secondary part, naming the telescopes that caused it. The named
telescopes get a SCRAPPED history row; the primary parts are untouched and wait for
the replacement secondary to catch up.

SecondaryMillJobHistoryOut.title: SecondaryMillJobHistoryOut
SecondaryMillJobHistoryOut.description:
One completed secondary-lane mill job *family* — the origin run
(`cloned_from_job_id IS NULL`) plus every REWORK re-run cloned from it — for the
Production History page's Milling Job History (Secondary) tab.

A REWORK clones the origin's job row rather than creating a new one
(`task_effects._rework_effects`), chaining `cloned_from_job_id` one link at a
time, so the family's time and telescope-iteration figures are rolled up onto the
origin's row here rather than appearing as separate rows of their own.

StepStateEnum.title: StepStateEnum
StepStateEnum.description: Where an order's step stands, read off the plan (spec decision 22).

SubjectDetail.title: SubjectDetail
SubjectDetail.description:
Structured facts about a task's subject, per subject kind, for the start modal.

Derived, not columns -- built by services/process/subject_detail. Which fields are
set depends on the kind: an AM job carries its print number and gold estimate, a
mill job its blank (primary) or plate (secondary), a plate its name, a set its
plates. `display_part_ids` is what to render under the subject -- usually the
proposal's own parts, but for the ORDER tail (INSPECTION, DOCUMENTATION,
PACKAGING_SHIPPING) every live part of the order, since those steps are seeded on
the SECONDARY route only and their `order_part_ids` would hide the primaries.

TaskHistoryOut.title: TaskHistoryOut
TaskHistoryOut.description:
One completed WorkTask instance — for the Production History page's Task
History tab, which aggregates these per task_type (and re-applies the shared
date-range filter) client-side, so a row's numbers stay a sum-of-sums rather than
an average-of-averages. Unlike the AM/Mill history tabs this endpoint returns raw
instances, not one row per finished job — see components/shared.ts on the frontend.

unit_kind/units reuse the same task_planning_params-driven scaling the capacity/KPI
report uses (estimates._scaling_for / estimates._resolve_units), so "Work Unit"
means the same thing here as it does there.

order_ids — every order this task instance touches: the order itself for an
ORDER-subject task (INSPECTION, DOCUMENTATION, ...), or every order reached via
its parts' TaskPart -> OrderPart link otherwise (mirrors production._order_work_minutes'
same two-path resolution). The frontend uses this to scope the per-task-type table
to the same completed-and-in-range order set list_order_kpis already filters to —
a task touching only orders outside that set is dropped client-side.

TelescopeDetail.title: TelescopeDetail
TelescopeDetail.description:
One telescope of a secondary part, as the QM and REWORK surfaces need it.

Derived, not columns -- like WorkTaskOut.lease_active, model_validate(part) alone
leaves this empty and the page silently renders no rows. Every route whose response
the QM or REWORK page reads must populate it (see rework_state.telescopes_for).

TelescopeHistoryEntry.title: TelescopeHistoryEntry
TelescopeHistoryEntry.description:
One completed QM round for a telescope: the force measured that round, and the
mill offset applied in response (None for a round that passed and was never sent
to REWORK). Pairs the two per round so a per-tooth force/offset table can use list
index as the column -- see rework_state.telescopes_for, which builds this from the
same PartReworkHistory row (newton set at QM, offset_um stamped later by REWORK).

TelescopeOffset.title: TelescopeOffset
TelescopeOffset.description: How much this rework pass takes off one telescope, in micrometres.

TelescopeOutcomeEnum.title: TelescopeOutcomeEnum
TelescopeOutcomeEnum.description:
Verdict on ONE telescope of a secondary part at QM.

OK       -- within tolerance, this telescope is finished.
REWORK   -- out of tolerance, must be re-milled. Becomes an *open rework request*
            until the REWORK task stamps rework_job_id on the row; the outcome
            itself is never rewritten, it is the audit record of that verdict.
SCRAPPED -- this telescope is why the whole secondary part was scrapped.

TelescopeResult.title: TelescopeResult
TelescopeResult.description:
One QM verdict on one telescope: the tooth of a secondary part, measured against
the primary part of the same tooth.

TimelineOrderOut.title: TimelineOrderOut
TimelineOrderOut.description: Lifecycle milestones of an order. Due / estimated are dates, the rest instants.

TimelineSendBackOut.title: TimelineSendBackOut
TimelineSendBackOut.description: A cancelled gate task carrying a send-back note; derived, no table of its own.

TimelineSessionOut.title: TimelineSessionOut
TimelineSessionOut.description:
One span a worker was on a task. An open session reads as ending at its last
heartbeat (end_reason None). `estimated` marks the single stand-in session drawn for a
legacy task that has none recorded.

ToothHeightInput.title: ToothHeightInput
ToothHeightInput.description: One tooth's height in mm. Limits mirror Tooth.height_mm, Numeric(5, 2).

UnitKindEnum.title: UnitKindEnum
UnitKindEnum.description:
Scaling granularity of a task/job duration.

PART is **teeth-weighted** (estimates.work_units -> len(part.teeth), min 1), so a
4-telescope secondary part counts as 4. PART_COUNT is a plain part count, where the
same part counts as 1. They are genuinely different questions -- QM is per telescope,
sawing is per part -- so do not substitute one for the other.

WorkSessionEndReason.title: WorkSessionEndReason
WorkSessionEndReason.description: Why a work session closed. NULL ended_at (still open) has no reason.

WorkTaskCorrectionOut.title: WorkTaskCorrectionOut
WorkTaskCorrectionOut.description:
One completed WorkTask, for the time-correction page's WorkTasks tab table,
outlier table, and scatter plot.

eta.title: Eta
eta.description:
When the unattended run is expected to end. Derived — the UI shows an overdue
marker past it.

WorkTaskTimeUpdate.title: WorkTaskTimeUpdate
WorkTaskTimeUpdate.description:
PATCH body for /process/time-correction/tasks/{task_id}. Only the fields
actually being corrected are sent -- read with model_dump(exclude_unset=True) so
an omitted field is left alone rather than treated as "clear to null".
